```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

For a large variant scan, fit the nuisance model once, calculate score tests
in batches, and reserve full TOP models for selected variants.

```{r data}
library(TOP)
data("data", package = "TOP")

y <- data[, 1:5]
variants <- data[, 6, drop = FALSE]
adjustment <- data[, 7, drop = FALSE]
```

## Fit reusable score support

`top_score_support()` fits the null model containing adjustment covariates.
The returned object can be reused for every batch with the same subjects,
outcomes, and nuisance model.

```{r support}
support <- top_score_support(
  y = y,
  additive = adjustment,
  missing_value = 888
)

support
```

## Scan variants

Each variant column is tested independently. The default additive structure
tests the baseline effect and all tumor-marker main effects jointly.

```{r scan}
scan <- top_score_scan(
  y = y,
  variants = variants,
  support = support,
  structure = "additive",
  missing_value = 888
)

as.data.frame(scan)
scan$score
```

For genome-wide data, pass manageable column batches while reusing `support`.

```{r batch-pattern, eval=FALSE}
all_results <- lapply(variant_batches, function(batch) {
  as.data.frame(top_score_scan(
    y = y,
    variants = batch,
    support = support,
    missing_value = 888
  ))
})
all_results <- do.call(rbind, all_results)
```

Singular information matrices are recorded in the `status` column with an
`NA` p-value, allowing a batch scan to continue.

## Fit selected variants

`top_followup()` fits one detailed Wald model per selected variant and extracts
variant-specific global association, global heterogeneity, and second-stage
effect results.

```{r followup}
followup <- top_followup(
  y = y,
  variants = variants,
  adjustment = adjustment,
  variant_structure = "additive",
  missing_value = 888,
  keep_models = FALSE
)

followup$results
followup$effects
```

Use `on_error = "record"` (the default) for several selected variants so a
single nonconvergent model is reported without discarding successful fits. Use
`keep_models = TRUE` when full fitted `top_model` objects are needed.
